newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey assessing Eregli sell-off bids.
newsitem.headline: Turkey assessing Eregli sell-off bids.

text.p: Turkey's privatisation administration (OIB) had begun assessing bids for the privatisation of the country's sole flat steel producer Eregli Demir Celik Fabrikalari, the OIB president said on Thursday.
"We received two bids for the privatisation of Eregli in December and work to evaluate the bids has begun," said OIB president Ismail Karakaya. He did not give other details.

The government, which holds 51.66 percent of the plant, plans to privatise 30-40 percent of Eregli through a bloc sale but will retain a golden share to ensure work continues on an imprpovement programme, to safeguard foreign debts guaranteed by the treasury and to protect the workers' jobs.

The two local bidders were Rumeli Metal, a company owned by the prominent Uzan family which has bought several cement plants from the government, and Zonguldak Yatrm, a joint investor group from Eregli town where the plant is located.
It is not clear when the OIB evaluation might be completed. The government plans to complete its privatisation this year.
The company will spend $88.604 million in 1997 for its continuing capacity increase and modernisation project (KAM), its annual report said.

The report, disclosed ahead of the blue-chip company's annual general meeting on Thursday, said Eregli would meet $53.3 million of the spending from its own resources and the rest through foreign loans for this year's investment in the KAM project.

The project, which will have an overall price tag of $1.53 billion when completed, was launched in 1990 to modernise the plant, Turkey's biggest, and to raise liquid and flat steel capacities by 50 percent to three million tonnes and 3.3 million tonnes respectively.
The report said the company, one of the centrepieces of the government's privatisation drive, had so far spent $1.4 billion for the project, which is nearly completed.
The company had a net profit of 6.2 trillion lira in 1996, down from 8.8 trillion lira a year ago, with net sales up to 73.7 trillion lira in 1996 from 33.8 trillion lira in 1995.
Eregli exported 501,706 tonnes of flat steel in 1996, mostly to Italy with 235,161 tonnes and the United States 78,507 tonnes, to earn a total of $150.13 million.
It produced 2,621,160 tonnes of flat steel in 1996, up from 1,632,615 tonnes in the previous year.
The report said Eregli was expecting world steel prices to rise from the second quarter of this year. "World steel markets will have more stability this year," it said.
Eregli shares, one of the mostly-traded shares on the Istanbul Stock Exchange, closed the morning trading at 17,250 lira, unchanged from Tuesday close.
